column2: Sir, does the Obscura understand these letters?
It does not understand anything. That is my responsibility.
Right, sir. Then I've brought this to you both.
You can hand it to the one with hands.
Sir, I've brought a coded message. The officer wants the readable version.
That is usually the arrangement. Give me the coded one first.
Sir, permission to interrupt? This needs deciphering.
You've already interrupted. You may as well give me a reason.
Here it is, sir. I believe the reason is somewhere in the cipher.
Then let's get it out.
Message from the wireless compartment, sir. Still in code.
Who is waiting for the result?
The watch officer, sir. He told me not to wander.
Then wait here while I examine it.
Sir, am I at the right station for decoding?
Unless you've brought something for the galley.
No sir. Definitely a message.
Then your navigation is satisfactory. Hand it over.
Sir, I carried this in my cap so it wouldn't get folded.
An unconventional filing system. Let me see the message.
Sir, the officer said to ask you what this means.
Did he say 'ask', or did he give you a message to have decoded?
The second one, sir. I was shortening it.
Keep the report accurate. I will deal with the shortening here.
Sir, can your machine turn this back into words?
With the proper settings and an operator, yes.
I suppose that's why they sent me to you instead of just to the machine.
A distinction I appreciate. Give me the paper.
Coded traffic for you, sir. I came as soon as they handed it to me.
Very well. Let us have a look at what arrived.
Sir, I was told not to let anyone else handle this.
You may make an exception for the man expected to decode it.
Yes sir. I wanted to hear that before letting go.
You have heard it. You may let go now.
Sir, I have a message. I don't know what it says.
That puts you in excellent company at this stage.
So it is supposed to look like that?
For now. Leave the decoding to me.
Sir, the radio watch asked for a clear copy of this.
They'll have my assessment once I've decoded it. Hand it over.
Sir, does decoding take longer if the message is important?
It takes longer if the messenger keeps asking questions.
I'll pass it over, sir.
An excellent way to begin.
Sir, the XO gave me this and pointed at your door.
A concise set of instructions.
I thought so too, sir. He looked busy, so I didn't ask for more.
I can take it from here. The paper, please.
Sir, they need this deciphered before they can discuss it.
Good. Discussion tends to work better after we know what was said.
Sir, I'm delivering this for decoding. Should I tell you who handed it to me?
Yes. Preferably before I have to ask.
The watch officer, sir. He is expecting me back with the result.
Then let me start.
Sir, may I ask something about the code on this paper?
You may ask me to decode it.
That's... actually what I was going to ask.
Then we have saved ourselves a security discussion. Hand it over.
Decoding request, sir. Everything they gave me is here.
Thank you. Keep it together while you pass it over.
Sir, this was handed to me with orders to find STASEC.
You've found STASEC. Now STASEC would like to see the message.
Of course, sir. Sorry, I was expecting another office.
We make economical use of the available offices.
Sir, I have some letters that apparently mean something.
Do you have them on paper?
Yes sir. I wasn't expected to remember them.
Good. I wasn't expecting you to either. Give it here.
Sir, the radioman told me to ask for decoding, not translation.
He has spared us both a small conversation. Let me see it.
Sir, I've been sent to collect the meaning of this message.
Leave the cipher with me first.
Yes sir. That did sound rather strange when I said it.
It was clear enough. Unlike the message, which I shall now examine.
Sir, am I interrupting something important? I have coded traffic.
At this desk, that qualifies as something important.
Shall I put it here, sir?
Yes. And take your elbow off the equipment.
Sir, is the decoded copy ready?
Ready and cleared. Take the papers back together.
Sir, it actually makes sense now.
That was the intention.
I meant that as a compliment, sir.
I shall accept it as one. Deliver the result.
Sir, can I report that the message is in order?
Yes. It has been decoded and accepted.
That's a report I won't mind making.
Then don't delay it on my account.
Sir, I didn't know what I was carrying until now.
You don't need to study it on the return journey either.
No sir. Straight to the officer.
Precisely. The message is ready.
Decoded successfully, sir?
Yes. Return it to the officer who sent you.
Sir, all those letters, and it comes out as a proper message.
The sender would have been disappointed otherwise.
I suppose the officer will be pleased to see it too.
Give him the opportunity. Take it back.
Sir, am I allowed to say the decoding went well?
You are allowed to report the result to your superior.
Only to my superior. Understood, sir.
Good. Everything is in order. Dismissed.
Sir, these two sheets are to travel together?
Yes. The decoded copy and its source. Keep them together.
Sir, may I ask how you knew which letters to use?
You may ask. I cannot explain the settings to you.
Well, it worked, sir. That's enough for me.
And the result is enough for your officer. Take it to him.
Sir, the watch officer will want to see this straight away.
It is decoded and cleared. There is nothing keeping you here.
Except that I was waiting to be dismissed, sir.
A sound habit. Dismissed.
Sir, would you call that a successful decoding?
Yes. You may call it that in your report as well.
Sir, should I fold the readable copy inside the other one?
Keep the contents out of sight and the papers together.
I can manage both, sir.
Then you are equipped for the journey. Off you go.
Sir, I understand now why this comes to your desk first.
An improvement over trying to read the cipher in the passageway.
I wasn't trying, sir. Not seriously.
Let us keep it that way. Take the cleared message back.
Everything satisfactory, sir?
Yes. The message has been decoded. You can return with the result.
Sir, does the Obscura ever get tired of doing this?
It has yet to file a complaint.
Neither will I, sir. Thank you for the decoded copy.
You're welcome. Deliver it before your superior files one.
Sir, I expect they'll ask if there were any problems.
Tell them the decoding is complete and the message is accepted.
Those exact words, sir?
They'll serve you better than an account of the machinery.
Sir, I can take this back now?
You can. The decoded message is cleared for delivery.
Sir, it's a relief to see ordinary words again.
Leave reading them to the intended recipient.
Of course, sir. I only meant the general appearance.
Then admire the general appearance of the passageway. Dismissed.
Sir, thank you. I wasn't sure how long this would take.
Neither was I until I started. It is done now.
I'll get it to the officer while he's still at his desk.
A sensible next step. Take both papers.
Sir, is there a particular way I should report this?
Message decoded, checks complete, result accepted. That will do.
Sir, it must be satisfying to get a proper message out of that jumble.
It is satisfying when it passes inspection as well. This one has.
A good result all round, then.
Provided it reaches the right hands. Attend to that part.
Sir, I think the officer was expecting a longer wait.
He can spend the time reading his message.
I won't tell him you said that, sir.
There is no need. Just give him the cleared copy.
Sir, shall I tell them STASEC has finished with it?
Yes. The message is decoded and in order.
Sir, was that a difficult one?
That question isn't part of your delivery instructions.
Just curiosity, sir. I'll take the result back.
Do that. The decoding is complete.
Sir, I have the source and the decoded sheet. Have I forgotten anything?
Where you're taking them, perhaps?
No sir. That part I remember very clearly.
Then you have everything you need. The message is accepted.
Sir, is it fair to say the message survived the trip through the machine?
Yes. I would keep the report a little more formal, though.
Sir, I suppose I shouldn't tell anyone what came out.
You should tell the officer waiting for it. Nobody else.
Understood. Accepted and decoded, delivered privately.
An admirable plan. Carry it out.
Sir, the chief will be glad to have something he can read.
Then I recommend taking him the decoded copy along with the source.
Both here, sir. I checked.
Good. Everything is in order. Return to your duty.
Sir, permission to return with the decoded message?
Granted. It is cleared. Keep the papers secure.
Sir, I was beginning to enjoy watching the lamps.
The lamps have finished their work. Have you?
Not until I've delivered this, sir.
Correct. The message is ready to go.
Sir, the message hasn't been accepted?
Correct. Report it as a FALSE ECHO. It is not to be acted upon.
Sir, I thought getting the words out was the whole job.
Getting words out doesn't make the message trustworthy.
I hadn't thought of that, sir.
That is why it comes here. Take back the rejection.
Sir, the officer is going to ask what he's supposed to do with this.
He is to treat it as rejected traffic, not as an instruction.
I'll make sure he hears that part clearly.
See that you do. Dismissed.
Sir, does this mean the machine broke?
It means I have rejected the message.
So I shouldn't report a fault with the Obscura?
You should report the decision I just gave you.
FALSE ECHO, sir. Have I understood correctly?
You have. Return with that result and keep the papers secure.
Sir, perhaps it would look better if I took a little longer going back.
Would that make the message any more acceptable?
No sir. Just me a little less available for questions.
Your superior needs the rejection promptly. Off you go.
Sir, should I apologize to the officer?
For carrying a message where you were ordered to carry it? No.
Then I'll simply give him the result.
The message is rejected. Keep it that simple.
Sir, can I tell them the message was no good?
Tell them it was rejected by STASEC. Use the proper wording.
Sir, should someone have noticed this before it reached you?
I am concerned with what leaves this desk. This leaves it rejected.
No assigning blame, sir. Just the result.
A useful distinction. Take it back.
Sir, the officer won't be pleased to hear it's a FALSE ECHO.
He would be less pleased to act on one without being told.
Yes sir. I hadn't put it that way.
You needn't put it any way. Report the rejection.
Sir, is there an accepted copy for me to deliver?
No. This message is rejected. That is what you are to report.
Sir, could they ask somebody else to decode it?
They could. My assessment would still have to be reported.
I wasn't suggesting we leave that part out, sir.
Then make certain it is the first thing you say.
Sir, ought I to warn the radio watch that something is wrong?
Report that this message has been rejected. Don't embellish it.
No alarm, no theories. Understood, sir.
Good. You can deliver a useful report without either.
Sir, am I taking back a FALSE ECHO?
Yes. Make sure the officer knows it has been rejected.
Sir, I don't relish being the one to bring this result back.
Would you prefer to leave your superior waiting for a message that won't be cleared?
No sir. That sounds considerably worse.
Then your course is clear. Report the rejection.
Sir, they'll want to know what you think the message really means.
What I think matters here is that it must not be accepted as valid traffic.
So no guesses about the contents?
None from you. Take the result to your superior.
Rejected, sir. May I return to the officer?
Yes. Tell him this message is not cleared for use.
Sir, they sounded quite certain this would be important.
Then it is important that they hear it was rejected.
I'll go straight back, sir.
And keep that assessment with the message.
Sir, does delivering this mean I'm involved in whatever is wrong with it?
It means you were the messenger. Don't promote yourself into a suspect.
I would rather not, sir.
Then finish your delivery. The message is rejected, not you.
Sir, what should I say if they ask whether they can use it anyway?
That STASEC rejected it. It is not an approved instruction.
Sir, would you explain the rejection to the chief if he asked?
I would discuss it with the chief. You are here to carry the result.
Understood. I won't try to explain it for you.
A considerable service to us both. Return the message.
Sir, I'm not sure they'll believe me when I say FALSE ECHO.
You are carrying the result from this station. You needn't win a debate.
I'll give them the papers, sir.
And tell them plainly that the message was rejected.
Sir, is there anything else I should collect?
You have the rejected message and the result. Take them back together.
Sir, I was hoping to leave here with good news.
You are leaving with an assessment. That was the purpose of the visit.
Yes sir. I'll leave the hoping out of my report.
It will be shorter and more accurate for it. Dismissed.
Sir, I suppose I should avoid repeating anything from this message.
You should avoid repeating message contents in any case.
Of course. I meant particularly this one.
This one is rejected. That is the information your superior needs.
Sir, shall I wait for a different result?
No. The assessment is complete. Report the message as rejected.
Sir, can a message look official and still end up like this?
You have just seen one rejected. Appearance isn't the whole assessment.
I'll remember that, sir.
For now, remember where you're taking the result.
Sir, should I tell the officer you were very firm about the rejection?
Tell him the message is rejected. My tone of voice isn't part of the report.
No sir. Just the assessment.
You have it. Return to your duty.
Sir, does FALSE ECHO mean we ignore that this ever arrived?
No. Report its arrival and its rejection. It is not valid traffic.
Sir, I'm trying to find a polite way of saying this was rejected.
'The message was rejected, sir' would cover it.
I was making it more complicated, wasn't I?
Considerably. Deliver that result while it is still fresh in your mind.
Don't get up. I need an assessment of this verification message.
At once, sir. I'll check it against the standing orders.
I have heard three opinions about this traffic. I would like one finding.
Yes sir. I'll verify the message and report the result.
Have a look at this. Something about it has been bothering me.
Is there a particular concern, sir?
There is. Whether we can trust it. Establish that first.
Understood, sir. I'll begin the verification.
